shortDescription: France's anti-cybercrime unit has closed two websites alleged to be selling stolen data and arrested three 17-year-olds suspected of running them, Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said in a statement on Friday.

children: France's anti-cybercrime unit has closed two websites alleged to be selling stolen data and arrested three 17-year-olds suspected of running them, Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said in a statement on Friday.
The Reacher platform was created in March and offered stolen personal data from different sources to the public through different kinds of subscriptions, the statement said
The service, which was renamed Stryx in June, claimed to store 730 million lines of data, including names, addresses and bank account numbers, and had received 3.1 million requests
The three male teenagers could face up to 10 years in prison, if convicted
